newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian FSB Bank raises capital base.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian FSB Bank raises capital base.

text.p: Shareholders of Nigeria's FSB International Bank on Thursday voted to increase its capital base with the approval of a scrip issue, the bank's chief executive officer, Mohammed Hayatu-Deen said.
Shareholders will now own eight new shares for every existing three.

"Based on our existing paid-up capital of 139.1 million naira, our bonus will bring our paid up capital to 510 million naira, a figure that will be in excess of the 500 million naira capital requirement of the Central Bank of Nigeria," said Hayatu-Deen.

Nigeria in January ordered banks to raise their capital to a minimum of 500 million naira by the end of next year. Before then, commercial banks were required to have a capital base of at least 50 million naira and merchant banks 40 million naira.
The authorities argue that the new minimum will lessen the risk of bank failures which plagued the West African nation in recent years.
FSB said it grossed 1.4 billion naira in the year to end-March, about double the 786.6 million naira for the previous year. Profit after tax rose to 433.6 million naira against 241.7 million naira.
The company said it would pay no dividend this year.
Its share price closed steady at 4.50 naira on the Thursday.
